newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-SODIGRAF NEED STRIKER TO FIND FORM AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SODIGRAF NEED STRIKER TO FIND FORM AGAIN.

text.p: Zaire's Mbuilua Tondelua needs to rediscover his goal touch if unfancied Sodigraf are to have any chance of an upset against Arab Contractors of Egypt in the African Cup Winners' Cup final.
The 25-year-old striker has scored nine goals for the Zairean club en route to the first leg of the final in Kinshasa on Sunday but just one since the second round.

Tondelua is the leading scorer in the three African club competitions this season and has emerged as one of the contiennt's exciting finds of the year, breaking into the Zaire national team and scoring in World Cup qualifiers.
But with just one goal in his last four Cup Winners' Cup matches, he looks flat after a long season just when his modest club need him the most.
"I could kick myself for not having scored lately," he said in a recent interview. "But in football you have to learn to adapt to all situations."
Sunday's match at the imposing Kamonyola stadium is Sodigraf's first appearance in an African club competition final and comes just two years after the club gained first division status in Zaire.
The team, originally the works side of a now-defunct brick-building factory, bought their first division status when they took over the franchise of a financially ailing club in the city.
They are coached by Lusadisu Basilwa, who was Zaire's caretaker coach at the African Nations Cup finals in South Africa in January.
Sodigraf's opponents will be seeking to set up the first part of an Egyptian one-two in Africa's top two club tournaments.
Arab Contractors are seeking a third African Cup Winners' Cup title while fellow Cairo club Zamalek set off in search of the African Champions' Cup next week.
Egypt and Cameroon are the only countries to have won the two major African tournaments in the same year.
Contractors, who have been struggling with their league form since September, will stage the return leg in Cairo on December 6.
